chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Umara, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Adam was descended to the earth, he needed food and drink, so he complained of that to Jibraeel (peace be upon him). Jibraeel said to him: 'O Adam, become a farmer.' He said: 'So teach me a supplication.' He said: 'Say: O Allah, suffice me with the provisions of the world and every horror before Paradise, and clothe me with health until livelihood becomes welcoming to me.'
ai.seo_question: What supplication did Jibraeel teach Adam for sustenance and health?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the theological merit of agriculture by linking Adam’s earthly sustenance directly to divine instruction via Jibraeel, thereby elevating farming from mere labor to an act of worship. The supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on seeking 'afiyah (comprehensive well-being) as the foundation for a contented life, framing agricultural work as a means to achieve spiritual and material sufficiency before the final entry into Paradise.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Umara, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Adam<sup>as</sup> was descended to the earth, he<sup>as</sup> became needy to the food and the drink. So that was grievous upon Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>. So Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘O Adam<sup>as</sup>! Become a farmer’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘So teach me<sup>as</sup> a supplication’. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘Say: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Suffice me<sup>as</sup> with the provisions of the world and (from) every horror before the Paradise, and Clothe me<sup>as</sup> with the good health until life becomes welcoming for me<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from al-Hassan ibn ‘Umarah from Misma’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When Adam descended to earth he needed food and drinks and he complained to Jibril. Jibril said to him, ‘O Adam, be a farmer.’ He said, ‘Teach me a prayer.’ Jibril said, ‘Say: “O Lord, protect me against the worldly impediments and all horrors that are before reaching paradise and dress me in good health so life becomes pleasant for me.’”
